candidates.original_title: The drunk utilitarian: Blood alcohol concentration predicts utilitarian responses in moral dilemmas
candidates.description: Pro-sacrificial harm judgments in the switch dilemma as a function of blood alcohol concentration
candidates.citation_sentence: For responses to the two variants of the trolley problem, we expected to obtain effects that correspond to Duke and Bègue's (2015) correlational findings.
candidates.notes: Preregistered experiment with N=329 found no significant effect of alcohol on moral judgments across all measures (all Fs and ts nonsignificant), failing to replicate the drunk utilitarian phenomenon originally reported by Duke and Bègue (2015). Original study was correlational; this replication was experimental with placebo control and higher alcohol dose.
